prompt: Create a system design for the supplied webhook-ingestion product. Customers POST signed events; events can be duplicated and delivered out of order; normal load is 50 events/s with 10-minute bursts to 2,000/s; accepted events must not be lost after the API returns success; per-customer processing order is required but global order is not; downstream enrichment can be unavailable for 20 minutes; p95 API acknowledgement must stay below 250 ms; the product needs replay for 7 days. Compare a synchronous processing design with a durable-ingest-plus-queue/worker design. Define trust and idempotency boundaries, durable state ownership, partition/order key, backpressure, retry/dead-letter/replay behavior, observability, failure isolation, and capacity assumptions. State the chosen architecture, rejected alternative, quality scenarios, tradeoffs, and which load/failure tests must validate the design before launch. Do not select named cloud services unless the supplied constraints require a specific provider.

requirements: signed customer webhook API with duplicate and out-of-order delivery
50 events/s normal and 2,000 events/s burst profile
acknowledged events cannot be lost and p95 acknowledgement target is 250 ms
per-customer ordering and seven-day replay are required
downstream enrichment may be unavailable for twenty minutes

falsifiableChecks.assertion: The acknowledgement boundary is tied to a durable state transition that makes the no-loss claim testable.
The design specifies how per-customer ordering, duplicates, retries, and replay interact without imposing unnecessary global ordering.
The plan states capacity/backpressure assumptions and concrete load/failure tests for the 2,000 events/s burst and 20-minute downstream outage.

evidence: requirements drive the topology rather than vendor fashion
failure and recovery behavior is explicit
unverified capacity claims are converted into planned evidence
